title: Add invocation stability index and noise-attenuation adapter
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Ops and SREs are spending a lot of time triaging transient token/latency spikes that are noisy (short-lived) and not indicative of systemic regressions. This PR introduces a lightweight per-invocation 'Invocation Stability Index' (ISI) and a downstream 'Noise Attenuation Adapter' for alert routing to reduce noisy alerts while preserving SLO-sensitive signals. Motivation: provide a single derived signal that captures dispersion in token latency, retry/early-termination rate, and KV-cache miss jitter so that alerting rules can differentiate stable regressions from ephemeral noise. Design summary: - Runtime: compute ISI (0-100) per invocation as a normalized aggregation of: latency variance across token phases, token-count jitter vs baseline, retry/early-termination events, and kv-cache-miss ratio. Implementation emits a span tag stability.score and a prometheus histogram redwood_invocation_stability_bucket with labels {route, model, tenant, region}. Cardinality controls: we explicitly avoid per-invocation IDs on metrics and only tag traces with invocation_id for post-hoc joins. - Alerting adapter: a middleware in alertd that consults short-term ISI rollups and applies dynamic suppression rules: if stability.avg_1m < 30 and spike duration < 2m, suppress non-critical alerts and route to 'quiet' channel for 10m; critical SLO alerts still bypass the adapter. The adapter records decisions in telemetry (noise_attenuator.decision{action=suppress|allow}). - Dashboards/UI: added Stability Cohorts panel (percent of invocations by ISI bucket), Stability Heatmap (route x time), and Noise Attenuation Actions table (recent suppressions, reason, affected routes). A compact StabilityBadge component shows in the Console invocation view. - Rollout: gated behind feature-flag rtev.stability_index. Canary plan: 1% (staging) -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days with SLO guardrails. - Performance: measured overhead in synthetic load tests: ~0.4ms median added p95 latency for runtime tagging and ~2% CPU for collectors under 50k invocations/s; metric cardinality kept low. - Tests: unit tests for scoring logic, property tests for normalization boundary cases, integration e2e that replays synthetic noisy spikes and validates suppression behavior; added load test scenario. - Docs: operational runbook explaining how to tune ISI thresholds and how to disable suppression per-tenant. Checklist: [x] Implementation of ISI in runtime and tracer enrichment | [x] Prometheus metrics and rollups | [x] Noise Attenuation Adapter and policy YAML | [x] Console panels and StabilityBadge | [x] Unit / integration / load tests | [x] Docs and runbook | [x] Feature flag and canary rollout plan Commit summary: (see commits field). Changed files (high-level): runtime/metrics (stability index), tracing (span enrichment), observability pipeline (adapter), dashboards and console components, docs, featureflag config. See changed_files list for specifics. Why unique: focuses on signal composition (stability index) + policy adapter to suppress alert noise rather than only adding more telemetry.

review_comments: Lucas Chen: Nice approach. Please ensure metric cardinality is bounded — drop invocation_id and avoid high-cardinality labels.
Maya Patel (author): Reworked metrics to only include {route,model,tenant,region}; retained invocation_id only on spans for trace joins.
Priya Natarajan: Can we reduce the suppression window to 2m max? Also suggest exponential backoff for repeated suppressions on the same route.
Maya Patel (author): Adjusted policy: transient window 2m, suppression TTL 10m, added per-route cooldown to avoid repeated suppressions. Updated docs accordingly.
Owen Li: Integration test failed once due to flakiness in trace enrichment — reran CI. Approving after CI green.
release_notes: Introduces an Invocation Stability Index (ISI) and a Noise Attenuation Adapter to reduce alert noise from transient token/latency spikes. Highlights: new stability metrics and dashboard, an alerting adapter that applies dynamic suppressions, and an operational runbook for tuning. Rollout behind feature flag rtev.stability_index.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash after approvals and CI green
qa_notes: QA exercised with synthetic spike scenarios; validated that SLO-critical alerts are never suppressed and that suppression decisions are logged. To reproduce locally run e2e-tests/observability/stability_noise_scenarios.yaml with feature flag enabled.
observability_impact: New metrics: redwood_invocation_stability_{bucket,sum,count} stored in TSDB; stability.score appears on spans. Low cardinality labels to avoid TSDB blowup. Added telemetry for noise_attenuator.decision to audit suppression decisions.
rollout_plan: Feature flag rtev.stability_index; canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 7 days with manual gates at each step. Monitor: stability cohort distribution, alert rate, suppressed_alerts_count, and latency p95. Rollback: flip feature flag off; adapter disabled immediately.
notes_for_ops: If suppression is causing missed regressions, set policy 'allow_all' and file ENG-1921 for follow-up. Policy files live in observability/adapter and are tenant-overridable.
examples_of_alert_rules_using_isi: - non-critical route spike rule: trigger if redwood_route_latency_p95 increase AND stability.avg_1m >= 40 -> route to standard channel. If stability.avg_1m < 30 and spike < 2m -> suppress to quiet channel.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Rollout canary per plan; 2) Schedule 24h alert reduction review with SRE; 3) Add per-tenant opt-out flag and document in onboarding; 4) Sweep dashboards for customers on Dedicated/Private to ensure visibility.
notes_unique_to_pr: This PR couples a derived score with an active adapter that mutates alert routing decisions; unlike previous work that only added telemetry, this change actively reduces noise by making suppression decisions based on a composite signal.
